newsitem.title: USA: Clinton sees no change in Cuba embargo policy.
newsitem.headline: Clinton sees no change in Cuba embargo policy.

text.p: President Bill Clinton said on Friday he saw no prospect of changing the hardline U.S. embargo policy against Cuba so long as Cuba "murdered" Americans.

"The Castro govenment illegally shot down two planes and murdered Americans," Clinton said in referring to a 1996 incident in which Cuban jets downed planes flown by Cuban-American demonstrators. "Our policy toward Cuba today therefore is one that is dicated by Cuba not by the United States. And until I see some indication of willingness to change it's going to be very difficult to persuade me to change our policy."

Clinton reaffired his tough stance toward Cuba -- one that has brought Washington into conflict with allies like Canada, Mexico and Western Europe over free-trade issues -- during an appearance at a meeting of the American Society of Newspaper Editors.

He rejected the premise of a questioner who suggested the United States might approach Cuba with the same give-and-take spirit it has shown Communist governments in China, Vietnam and North Korea. "The other three countries you mention have not murdered any Americans lately," he retorted.
He noted that the fatal aerial episode involving Florida-based anti-Castro Cubans flying unarmed planes near Cuba's coast had followed America's brief adoption of the so-called Cuban Democracy Act.

The Act, which Clinton supported as a presidential candidate in 1992, established a "two-track" policy towards Cuba by barring foreign-based subsidiaries of U.S. companies from trading with Havana but also promoting "people to people" contacts between Americans and Cubans.

Clinton said the plane episode outraged Americans and prompted Congress to "change our policy" by passing the Helms-Burton law, which establishes penalties against even foreign firms that invest in Cuba. That law has drawn widespread condemnation from U.S. allies. "I signed it regretfully but not reluctantly," he said.
